chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul A'ala who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The bearing of our matter is not merely affirming it and accepting it; from the bearing of our matter is veiling it and safeguarding it from those not deserving of it. So convey greetings to them and say to them: May Allah have mercy on a servant who attracts the affection of people to himself. Narrate to them what they know, and conceal from them what they deny.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, the one who establishes war with weapons against us is not more burdensome to us than the speaker who speaks against us with what we dislike. So when you recognize a broadcast from a servant, go to him and repel him from it. If he accepts from you, fine; otherwise, load upon him with one who is heavy upon him, and he will listen to him.'

For indeed, a man from you seeks a need and is gentle/moderate in it until it is fulfilled for him. So be gentle/moderate regarding my need as you are regarding your own needs. If he accepts from you, fine; otherwise, bury his words under your feet and do not say, 'He says, and he says,' for that would be borne upon me and upon you. And by Allah, if you were saying what I say, I would acknowledge that you are my companions.

This is Abu Hanifa, for whom there are companions, and this is Al-Hasan Al-Basri, for whom there are companions. And I am a man from Quraish, born to me by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). I know the Book of Allah, and therein is the explanation of everything: the beginning of creation, the matters of the sky, the matters of the earth, the matters of the former ones, the matters of the latter ones, the matters of what was, and the matters of what will be. It is as if I am looking at that established before my eyes.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'concealment' (satr) in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the doctrine of *Satr* (concealment) as a dynamic political and theological strategy, distinguishing passive belief from active protection of the Imamate from the 'unworthy' (*ghayr ahliha*). It highlights the practical wisdom of tailoring discourse to the audience's capacity, warning that indiscriminate dissemination of teachings burdens both the speaker and the listener, a concept central to Shia epistemology during periods of political oppression. The Imam’s assertion of his Qurayshi lineage and comprehensive knowledge of the Quran underscores the divine authority (*Hujjiyyah*) inherent in the Ahl al-Bayt.
